question: Implementing the obligation concerning the digitalisation of traceability data laid down by Regulation (EU) 2023/2842

Pursuant to the Fisheries Control Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2023/2842), the sector’s traceability data will have to be digitalised as of 10 January 2026. However, this deadline is unrealistic for many operators given the absence of a harmonised EU technical framework.

The fact that the Commission withdrew all articles concerning digitalisation from its latest proposal for a delegated act supplementing the Fisheries Control Regulation is testament to how challenging this process will be. In the notice accompanying its proposal, the Commission stated that it will organise a series of technical meetings to specify how digitalisation will be implemented in practice.

The EC has also commissioned a study on this topic. In addition, the French fisheries sector is actively working to establish a robust traceability system to ensure that catch data are shared with actors at the end of the supply chain. It is therefore clear that rushing digitalisation could hamper the development of a common EU tool. 1.
When will the technical meetings the Commission mentioned in the aforementioned notice take place, and what form will they take?
What tool will the Commission use to specify the technical arrangements for implementing the digitalisation of traceability data?
Is the Commission planning to postpone the date on which the digitalisation obligation will enter into force?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.1.2026) Informal targeted consultations of stakeholders have already started and will be followed by a public consultation, planned for the first half of 2026. A technical meeting with Member States experts is scheduled for the first quarter of 2026.

The Commission underlines that compliance with Article 58(6) of Regulation (EU) 2023/28421 operates independently of the adoption of any supplementing legislation. Moreover, the co-legislators did not envisage any mandatory use of the empowerment under Article 58(12) of Regulation (EC) No 1224/20092.

The obligation to make information available ‘in a digital way’ is formulated broadly, allowing compliance through a range of means that enable digital data transmission. Finally, the Commission does not have the power, through delegated legislation, to postpone the 2026 implementation deadline established by the co-legislators in Regulation (EU) 2023/2842.

The Commission will continue working with stakeholders and Member States to develop supplementary rules that can support them and further harmonise and simplify the traceability framework, without undermining the policy objectives of the revised fisheries control regulation.
